resources.desc: Overview of the RollJam rolling code exploitation device.

resources.name: IOActive's Tools and Data
resources.desc: Chris Valasek and Charlie Miller release some of their tools and data for hacking into vehicles in an effort to get more people into vehicle security research.

resources.name: Developments in Car Hacking
resources.desc: via the SANS Reading Room, Currie's paper analyses the risks and perils of smart vehicle technology.

resources.name: Car Hacking on the Cheap
resources.desc: A whitepaper from Chris Valasek and IOActive on hacking your car when you don't have a lot of resources at your disposal.

resources.name: Car Hacking: The definitive source
resources.desc: Charlie Miller and Chris Valasek publish all tools, data, research notes, and papers for everyone for free

resources.name: Car Hacking on the cheap

resources.name: Researchers tackle autonomous vehicle security

resources.name: Reverse engineering of the Nitro OBD2
resources.desc: Reverse engineering of CAN diagnostic tools.

resources.name: Analysis of an old Subaru Impreza - Subaru Select Monitor v1 (SSM1)
resources.desc: Digging into an old ECU through an old protocol and disabling a 1997 Subaru Impreza's speed limiter.

resources.name: Car Hacking in 30 Minutes or Less
resources.desc: Using VirtualBox and Kali Linux, you can start car hacking using completely free open-source software and tools, including can-utils, ICSim, ScanTool, Wireshark, and tcpdump

resources.name: "Hopping on the CAN Bus" from BlackHat Asia 2015
resources.desc: A talk from BlackHat Asia 2015 that aims to enable the audience to "gain an understanding of automotive systems, but will also have the tools to attack them".

resources.name: "Drive It Like You Hacked It" from DEFCON 23
resources.desc: A talk and slides from Samy Kamkar's DEFCON 23/2015 talk that includes hacking garages, exploiting automotive mobile apps, and breaking rolling codes to unlock any vehicle with low cost tools.

resources.name: Samy Kamkar on Hacking Vehicles with OnStar
resources.desc: Samy Kamkar, the prolific hacker behind the Samy worm on MySpace, explores hacking into vehicles with OnStar systems.

resources.name: Remote Exploitation of an Unaltered Passenger Vehicle
resources.desc: DEFCON 23 talk Chris Valasek and Charlie Miller give their now famous talk on hacking into a Jeep remotely and stopping it dead in its tracks.

resources.desc: DEFCON 21 talk by Chris Valasek and Charlie Miller on automotive networks.

resources.name: Can You Trust Autonomous Vehicles?
resources.desc: DEFCON 24 talk by Jianhao Liu, Chen Yan, Wenyuan Xu

resources.name: Ken Munro & Dave Lodge - Hacking the Mitsubishi Outlander & IOT
resources.desc: talk from BSides Manchester 2016 by Ken and Dave of Pen Test Partners

resources.name: FREE-FALL: HACKING TESLA FROM WIRELESS TO CAN BUS
resources.desc: Zeronights 2016 and later BlackHat talk by Sen Nie, Ling Liu, and Yuefeng Du from Tencent and KEEN Security lab

resources.name: Car Hacking 101
resources.desc: Bugcrowd LevelUp 2017 by Alan Mond

resources.name: State of Automotive Cyber Safety, 2015
resources.desc: State of automotive hacking, policy, industry changes, etc. from I Am The Cavalry track at BSides Las Vegas, 2015.

resources.name: State of Automotive Cyber Safety, 2016
resources.desc: State of automotive hacking, policy, industry changes, etc. from I Am The Cavalry track at BSides Las Vegas, 2016.

resources.name: How to Hack a Tesla Model S
resources.desc: DEF CON 23 talk by Marc Rogers and Kevin Mahaffey on hacking a Tesla. Tesla Co-Founder and CTO, JB Straubel, joins them to thank them and present a challenge coin.

resources.name: Car Hacking Videos
resources.desc: A web page with a long list of videos (40+) that are available online related to the topic of car hacking. From a 2007 DEF CON talk on modding engine ECUS and onwards (e.g. the 2017 Keen Security Tesla hack).

resources.name: Self-Driving and Connected Cars: Fooling Sensors and Tracking Drivers
resources.desc: Black Hat talk by Jonathan Petit. Automated and connected vehicles are the next evolution in transportation and will improve safety, traffic efficiency and driving experience. This talk will be divided in two parts: 1) security of autonomous automated vehicles and 2) privacy of connected vehicles. 2015

resources.name: A Survey of Remote Automotive Attack Surfaces
resources.desc: Black Hat talk By Charlie Miller and Chris Valasek. Automotive security concerns have gone from the fringe to the mainstream with security researchers showing the susceptibility of the modern vehicle to local and remote attacks. Discussion of vehicle attack surfaces. 2014.

resources.name: Pentesting vehicles with YACHT (Yet Another Car Hacking Tool)
resources.desc: A presentation that discusses different attack surfaces of a vehicle, then continues to describe an approach to car hacking along with tools needed to analyse and gather useful information.

resources.name: How to drift with any car
resources.desc: Introduction to CAN hacking, and using a real car as an Xbox controller.

resources.name: Car Infotainment Hacking Methodology and Attack Surface Scenario
resources.desc: A guide on how to attack, hunt bugs or hack your IVI by Jay Turla which was presented at the Packet Hacking Village / Wall of Sheep during DEF CON 26.

resources.name: TR19: Automotive Penetration Testing with Scapy
resources.desc: Overview on how Scapy can be used for automotive penetration testing at Troopers Conference 2019.

resources.name: Analysis and Defense of Automotive Networks
resources.desc: Overview of CAN, security, and potential intrusion detection approaches at BSides Knoxville 2020

resources.name: Remote Exploitation of Honda Cars
resources.desc: The Honda Connect app used by Honda City 5th generation used weak security mechanisms in its APIs for access control which would allow a malicious user to perform actions like starting the car, locking/unlocking car etc. remotely by interacting with it's Telematics Control Unit (TCU)

resources.name: TR22: UDS Fuzzing and the Path to Game Over
resources.desc: UDS diagnostics protocol fuzzing methodology, presented as a result of numerous penetration testing projects in the automotive industry, with real world exploitation PoCs, presented during Troopers Conference 2022.

resources.name: CCC - Horror Stories From the Automotive Industry
resources.desc: Horrifying examples of common vulnerabilities in the automotive industry, result of more than 100 penetration tests targeting Tier 1 suppliers and OEMs, with ultimate goal to raise awareness on the current state of automotive security. Additionally, PoC of automated week seed randomness exploitation in automotive components, by using a battery isolator in heavy-duty vehicles and the UDS protocol, for complete compromise of a target. Presented in Chaos Communication Camp, DeepSec 2023 and Troopers Conference 23.

resources.name: Car Hacking Scene in the PH: How Far We've Come
resources.desc: Car Hacking Village PH presents their first attempt on the main tracks for ROOTCON. This is a rundown of CHVPH's past security research to current research - from hacking infotainment systems to CAN Bus protocols and a summary of cars available in the Philippines which are susceptible to car thefts.

resources.name: Analysis of an In-vehicular network: From CAN bus to infotainment
resources.desc: This talk will feature Div0 CSQ’s 3 test benches as they explore more features on Connected vehicles. This was presented in ROOTCON 17 Car Hacking Village.

resources.name: An overview of Automotive Defensive Engineering
resources.desc: This talk is for car hackers to learn about modern defense measures being added to ECUs and Vehicle Architectures. This was presented in ROOTCON 17 Car Hacking Village.

resources.name: Hacking Back Your Car
resources.desc: Kamel Ghali's talk on ROOTCON 17 about how an attacker's perspective on hacking a car and origins of such attacks, how they've been used in different countries over the years, and explore the technical details of what makes such an attack possible.

resources.name: TR23: V2GEvil: Ghost in the wires
resources.desc: This research is dedicated to enhancing the cybersecurity of electric vehicles, with a specific focus on identifying vulnerabilities in the Electric Vehicle Communication Controller (EVCC), and an introduction to the tool V2GEvil. Accessible through the On-Board Charging (OBC) port, makes this attack vector really important for the security of future vehicles.

resources.name: DEF CON CHV - V2GEvil: Ghost in the wires
resources.desc: Shortened and summarized version of the talk V2GEvil: Ghost in the wires, from the DEF CON 32 Car Hacking Village, by Pavel Khunt and Thomas Sermpinis.

resources.name: The hack, the crash and two smoking barrels. (And all the times I (almost) killed an engineer.)
resources.desc: Thomas Sermpinis goes through the process of responsibly disclosing findings affecting the Blind Spot Detection Sensor of a current MY vehicle from one of the biggest OEMs in the world, leading to accusations that he was collaborating with hostile nations by the OEM. A story about how automotive manufacturers are treating the security industry, where are we heading, and how to be better, on the stage of DEF CON 32.

resources.name: 2014 Car Hacker's Handbook
resources.desc: Free guide to hacking vehicles from 2014.

resources.name: 2016 Car Hacker's Handbook
resources.desc: Latest version of the Car Hacker's handbook with updated information to hack your own vehicle and learning vehicle security. For a physical copy as well unlimited PDF, MOBI, and EPUB copies of the book, buy it at No Starch Press. Sections are available online here.

resources.name: A Comprehensible Guide to Controller Area Network
resources.desc: An older book from 2005, but still a comprehensive guide on CAN buses and networking in vehicles.

resources.name: Controller Area Network Prototyping with Arduino
resources.desc: This book guides you through prototyping CAN applications on Arduinos, which can help when working with CAN on your own car.

resources.name: Embedded Networking with CAN and CANopen
resources.desc: From 2003, this book fills in gaps in CAN literature and will educate you further on CAN networks and working with embedded systems.

resources.desc: OWASP's project to secure IoT, from cars to medical devices and beyond.

resources.name: Carloop Community
resources.desc: Community of people interested in car hacking and connecting vehicles to the cloud.

resources.name: Python Security
resources.desc: A website for browsing and buying python-integrated cars having certain vehicular security features.

resources.name: NIST Automotive Cybersecurity Community of Interest
resources.desc: NIST, the organization behind the NVD CVE database and modern cryptographic standards, runs a Community of Interest group for Automotive Cybersecurity that seeks to "provide a way for NIST to facilitate the discussions and receive comments and feedback from the automotive industry, academia, and government.".

resources.name: escar conference
resources.desc: Embedded security in cars. European event has run for over 10 years, and they now have US and Asia events.

resources.name: IT Security for Vehicles
resources.desc: Conference run by the Association of German Engineers (VDI), with participation from US and European OEMs, Tier 1s, and others.

resources.name: Cyber Truck Challenge
resources.desc: Conference that focuses on heavy vehicle cybersecurity issues. Includes hands-on assessments of heavy vehicles and subsystems.

resources.name: Security Weekly
resources.desc: Excellent podcast covering all ranges of security, with some episodes focusing portions on vehicle security from cars to drones.

resources.name: TrustedSec Podcast
resources.desc: From the people at TrustedSec, leaders in Social Engineering, their episodes often go into recent vehicle vulnerabilities and exploits.

resources.name: SANS Internet Storm Center
resources.desc: the ISC run a regular podcast going into the latest vulnerabilities and security news.

resources.name: Security Ledger
resources.desc: A podcast focusing on interviewing security experts about topics related to security.

resources.name: Car Hacking with Craig Smith
resources.desc: Software Engineering Daily did an amazing episode with Craig Smith, author of the Car Hacking Handbook (above), on hacking into vehicles.

resources.name: Big Bugs Podcast Episode 1: Auto Bugs - Critical Vulns found in Cars with Jason Haddix
resources.desc: Jason Haddix explores major vulnerabilities found in cars.

resources.name: Hacking Under the Hood and Into Your Car
resources.desc: Chris Valasek and Charlie Miller discuss with NPR how they were able to hack into vehicles.

resources.name: Hacking Connected Vehicles with Chris Valasek of IOActive
resources.desc: Chris Valasek talks about hacking into connected vehicles.

resources.name: Real ORNL Automotive Dynamometer (ROAD) CAN Intrusion Dataset
Open Vehicle Monitoring System
resources.desc: A community project building a hardware module for your car, a server to talk to it, and a mobile app to talk to the server, in order to allow developers and enthusiasts to add more functionality to their car and control it remotely.

resources.name: Open Source Car Control Project
resources.desc: The Open Source Car Control Project is a hardware and software project detailing the conversion of a late model vehicle into an autonomous driving research and development vehicle.

resources.name: Uptane
resources.desc: Uptane is an open and secure software update system design protecting software delivered over-the-air to the computerized units of automobiles and is designed to be resilient even to the best efforts of nation state attackers.

resources.name: Arduino
resources.desc: Arduino boards have a number of shields you can attach to connect to CAN-enabled devices.

resources.name: arduino-canbus-monitor
resources.desc: No matter which shield is selected you will need your own sniffer. This is implementation of standard Lawicel/SLCAN protocol for Arduino + any MCP CAN Shield to use with many standard CAN bus analysis software packages or SocketCAN

resources.name: CANtact
resources.desc: "The Open Source Car Tool" designed to help you hack your car. You can buy one or make your own following the guide here.

resources.name: Freematics OBD-II Telematics Kit
resources.desc: Arduino-based OBD-II Bluetooth adapter kit has both an OBD-II device and a data logger, and it comes with GPS, an accelerometer and gyro, and temperature sensors.

resources.name: ELM327
resources.desc: The de facto chipset that's very cheap and can be used to connect to CAN devices.

resources.name: GoodThopter12
resources.desc: Crafted by a well-known hardware hacker, this board is a general board that can be used for exploration of automotive networks.

resources.name: USB2CAN
resources.desc: Cheap USB to CAN connector that will register a device on linux that you can use to get data from a CAN network.

resources.name: Rinho Telematics
resources.desc: GPS trackers with native CAN Bus (J1939/FMS), WiFi fallback for offline data download, and BLE 5.0 sensors. Compatible with Traccar and Wialon.

resources.name: Intrepid Tools
resources.desc: Expensive, but extremely versatile tools specifically designed for reversing CAN and other vehicle communication protocols.

resources.name: Red Pitaya
resources.desc: Replaces expensive measurement tools such as oscilloscopes, signal generators, and spectrum analyzers. Red Pitaya has LabView and Matlab interfaces, and you can write your own tools and applications for it. It even supports extensions for things like Arduino shields.

resources.name: ChipWhisperer
resources.desc: A system for side-channel attacks, such as power analysis and clock glitching.

resources.name: HackerSDR
resources.desc: A Software Defined Radio peripheral capable of transmission or reception of radio signals from 1 MHz to 6 GHz. Designed to enable test and development of modern and next generation radio technologies.

resources.name: Carloop
resources.desc: Open source development kit that makes it easy to connect your car to the Internet. Lowest cost car hacking tool that is compatible with SocketCAN and can-utils. No OBD-II to serial cable required.

resources.name: CANBadger
resources.desc: A tool for reverse-engineering and testing automotive systems. The CANBadger consists of both hardware and software. The main interface is a LPC1768/LPC1769 processor mounted on a custom PCB, which offers two CAN interfaces, SD Card, a blinky LED, some GPIO pins, power supply for peripherals and the ethernet port.

resources.name: CANSPY
resources.desc: A platform giving security auditors to audit CAN devices. It can be used to block, forward or modify CAN frames on the fly autonomously as well as interactively.

resources.name: CANBus Triple
resources.desc: General purpose Controller Area Network swiss army knife and development platform.

resources.name: USBtin
resources.desc: USBtin is a simple USB to CAN interface. It can monitor CAN busses and transmit CAN messages. USBtin implements the USB CDC class and creates a virtual comport on the host computer.

resources.name: OpenXC
resources.desc: OpenXC is a combination of open source hardware and software that lets you extend your vehicle with custom applications and pluggable modules. It uses standard, well-known tools to open up a wealth of data from the vehicle to developers. Started by researchers at Ford, it works for all 2002 and newer MY vehicles (standard OBD-II interface). Researchers at Ford Motor Company joined up to create a standard way of creating aftermarket software and hardware for vehicles.

resources.name: Macchina M2
resources.desc: Macchina 2.0 is a complete overhaul of our 1.X generation of Macchina. The goals are still the same: Create an easy-to-use, fully-open, and super-compatible automotive interface.

resources.name: PandwaRF
resources.desc: PandwaRF is a pocket-sized, portable RF analysis tool operating the sub-1 GHz range. It allows the capture, analysis and re-transmission of RF via an Android device or a Linux PC. Capture any data in ASK/OOK/MSK/2-FSK/GFSK modulation from the 300-928 MHz band.

resources.name: CAN MITM Bridge by MUXSCAN
resources.desc: a tool to MITM CAN messages, allowing easy interaction with your car.

resources.name: PiCCANTE
resources.desc: Open-source CAN hacking tool based on Raspberry Pi Pico [2] (W) - Up to 3x CAN interfaces, includes ELM327 emulator.

resources.name: AutoPi
resources.desc: Open-source core software for the AutoPi dongle, a Raspberry Pi-based OBD-II device for vehicle telematics, CAN bus data collection, and automotive IoT applications.

resources.name: Wireshark
resources.desc: WireShark can be used for reversing CAN communications.

resources.name: Kayak
resources.desc: Java application for CAN bus diagnosis and monitoring.

resources.name: UDSim
resources.desc: GUI tool that can monitor a CAN bus and automatically learn the devices attached to it by watching communications.

resources.name: RomRaider
resources.desc: An open source tuning suite for the Subaru engine control unit that lets you view and log data and tune the ECU.

resources.name: O2OO
resources.desc: Works with the ELM327 to record data to a SQLite database for graphing purposes. It also supports reading GPS data. You can connect this to your car and have it map out using Google Maps KML data where you drive.

resources.name: CANToolz
resources.desc: CANToolz is a framework for analysing CAN networks and devices. It is based on several modules which can be assembled in a pipeline.

resources.name: BUSMASTER
resources.desc: An Open Source tool to simulate, analyze and test data bus systems such as CAN, LIN, FlexRay.

resources.name: BlackFlag ECU
resources.desc: Professional ECU diagnostics and tuning suite with OBD-II scanning, DTC reading, live sensor monitoring, and reflash capabilities.

resources.name: OpenXC
resources.desc: Currently, OpenXC works with Python and Android, with libraries provided to get started.

resources.name: openpilot
resources.desc: openpilot is an open source driving agent that performs the functions of Adaptive Cruise Control (ACC) and Lane Keeping Assist System (LKAS) for Hondas and Acuras.

resources.name: openalpr
resources.desc: An open source Automatic License Plate Recognition library written in C++ with bindings in C#, Java, Node.js, Go, and Python.

resources.name: metasploit
resources.desc: The popular metasploit framework now supports Hardware Bridge sessions, that extend the framework's capabilites onto hardware devices such as socketcan and SDR radios.

resources.name: Mazda AIO Tweaks
resources.desc: All-in-one installer/uninstaller for many available Mazda MZD Infotainment System tweaks.

resources.name: mazda_getInfo
resources.desc: A PoC that the USB port is an attack surface for a Mazda car's infotainment system and how Mazda hacks are made (known bug in the CMU).

resources.name: talking-with-cars
resources.desc: CAN related scripts, and scripts to use a car as a gamepad

resources.name: CANalyzat0r
resources.desc: A security analysis toolkit for proprietary car protocols.

resources.name: Tesla Mod
resources.desc: Tesla CAN bus toolkit for Flipper Zero and ESP32. Nag killer, FSD region unlock, track mode, BMS dashboard, blind spot alert, high beam strobe, and 30+ more CAN handlers. Open source (GPL-3.0).

resources.name: SocketCAN Utils
resources.desc: Userspace utilites for SocketCAN on Linux.

resources.name: vircar
resources.desc: a Virtual car userspace that sends CAN messages based on SocketCAN

resources.name: dbcc
resources.desc: "dbcc is a program for converting a DBC file primarily into into C code that can serialize and deserialize CAN messages." With existing DBC files from a vehicle, this file allows you to convert them to C code that extracts the CAN messages and properties of the CAN environment.

resources.name: High Level ViWi Service
resources.desc: High level Volkswagen CAN signaling protocol implementation.

resources.name: CanCat
resources.desc: A "swiss-army knife" for interacting with live CAN data. Primary API interface in Python, but written in C++.

resources.name: CANdevStudio
resources.desc: Development tool for CAN bus simulation. CANdevStudio enables to simulate CAN signals such as ignition status, doors status or reverse gear by every automotive developer.

resources.name: UnlockECU
resources.desc: Free, open-source ECU seed-key unlocking tool.

resources.name: ITS Geonetworking
resources.desc: ETSI ITS G5 GeoNetworking stack, in Java: CAM-DENM / ASN.1 PER / BTP / GeoNetworking

resources.name: CANard
resources.desc: A Python framework for Controller Area Network applications.

resources.name: Caring Caribou
resources.desc: Intended to be the *nmap of vehicle security*.

resources.name: c0f
resources.desc: A fingerprinting tool for CAN communications that can be used to find a specific signal on a CAN network when testing interactions with a vehicle.

resources.name: Python-CAN
resources.desc: Python interface to various CAN implementations, including SocketCAN. Allows you to use Python 2.7.x or 3.3.x+ to communicate over CAN networks.

resources.name: Python-OBD
resources.desc: A Python module for handling realtime sensor data from OBD-II vehicle ports. Works with ELM327 OBD-II adapters, and is fit for the Raspberry Pi.

resources.name: Scapy
resources.desc: A python library to send, receive, edit raw packets. Supports CAN and automotive protocols: see the automotive doc

resources.name: CanoPy
resources.desc: A python gui used to visualize and plot message payloads in real time.

resources.name: canTot
resources.desc: A python-based cli framework based on sploitkit and is easy to use because it similar to working with Metasploit. This similar to an exploit framework but focused on known CAN Bus vulnerabilities or fun CAN Bus hacks.

resources.name: Jumpstarter
resources.desc: A hardware-in-the-loop testing framework with automotive diagnostic drivers for UDS, DoIP, and CAN bus protocols.

resources.name: Caring Caribou Next
resources.desc: Upgraded and optimized version of the original Caring Caribou project.

resources.name: canarchy
resources.desc: CANarchy is a stream-first CAN analysis and manipulation runtime designed for automation, security research, and agent-driven workflows.

resources.name: CANNiBUS
resources.desc: A Go server that allows a room full of researchers to simultaneously work on the same vehicle, whether for instructional purposes or team reversing sessions.

resources.name: CAN Simulator
resources.desc: A Go based CAN simulator for the Raspberry Pi to be used with PiCAN2 or the open source CAN Simulator board

resources.name: NodeJS extension to SocketCAN
resources.desc: Allows you to communicate over CAN networks with simple JavaScript functions.

resources.name: UberATC
resources.desc: Uber Advanced Technologies Center, now Uber AV - <info@uberatc.com>.

resources.name: Tesla
resources.desc: Tesla hires security professionals for a variety of roles, particularly securing their vehicles.

resources.name: Intrepid Control Systems
resources.desc: Embedded security company building tools for reversing vehicles.

resources.name: Rapid7
resources.desc: Rapid7 does work in information, computer, and embedded security.

resources.name: IOActive
resources.desc: Security consulting firm that does work on pentesting hardware and embedded systems.

resources.name: Cohda Wireless
resources.desc: V2X DSRC Radio and Software

resources.name: VicOne
resources.desc: A subsidiary of Trend Micro which focuses on automotive security

resources.name: ASRG
resources.desc: The ASRG Disclosure Process is to support responsible disclosure when direct communication with the responsible company is unavailable or not responsive.

resources.name: Zeekr
resources.desc: Zeekr and Geely Responsible disclosure program
